title: Stock, profit and one workbook for your whole business
course_title: Excel and Google Sheets for Small Business

say: Stock, profit, and one workbook for your whole business.
This is the video for Module 4 of Excel and Google Sheets for Small Business.
Stock is often the biggest amount of money a small trader has tied up. An inventory sheet tells you what you have, what it is worth, and what to reorder before customers find empty shelves.

say: Set a reorder level for each product. If closing stock falls to that level, IF shows the word Reorder. Your sheet becomes an automatic shopping list.

say: Stock value is closing stock times cost price.
For example, Funke has 6 detergents left, and her reorder level is 8, so it says Reorder. Her stock on hand is worth 80250 naira at cost.

say: On your Sales tab, type just the product code, and let a lookup fetch the price. XLOOKUP finds the code in the Code column and returns the selling price from the same row. If the code is P03, it returns 3300.

panel.heading: Fetch the price from a code

say: If your Excel is 2019 or older, use VLOOKUP. The code must be in the first column of the table.
And always finish with FALSE. Leaving it out can quietly return the wrong product's price. If you see hash N A, the code was not found. Check for a letter O typed instead of a zero.

panel.heading: Fetch the price from a code

say: Now profit. Sales is the money earned from selling. Cost of goods sold is what the goods you actually sold cost you: opening stock value, plus purchases, minus closing stock value.
Why not sales minus purchases? Because if you stock up heavily, the month looks like a loss even though the goods are still on your shelves.

panel.heading: From sales to net profit
items: Sales: money earned from selling
Cost of goods sold: what the sold goods cost
Gross profit: sales minus cost of goods
Net profit: gross profit minus running costs
Margin: profit divided by sales

say: Gross profit is sales minus cost of goods. Net profit takes away running costs too, like rent, transport, data and power.

say: A margin divides profit by sales, so you can compare months of different sizes.

say: Here is Funke's October. She opened with stock worth 95000, bought 310000 more, and closed with 80250.
Her sales were 412000 naira. So her cost of goods sold is 324750.
Gross profit is 87250, a gross margin of 21.2%.
Rent share, transport, phone data and power come to 50000.
Net profit is 37250 naira. Of every 100 naira of sales, about 9 naira is net profit. That is up 6250 on September.
Running costs like rent and transport go in operating expenses.

panel.heading: Drawings are not an expense
right: Money you take for your household

say: But money you take out for yourself or your household is not a business expense. Record it as Drawings and leave it out. Otherwise the report hides how much the business really earns, and whether it can afford to pay you.

panel.heading: Drawings are not an expense

say: Put all your tabs in one workbook, and keep a simple routine.
Daily, 5 to 10 minutes, record every sale and expense. Weekly, run your check cell, look at the Reorder list and chase unpaid sales.
Monthly, count your shelves, make the profit report and download a backup. Quarterly, look at three months together and make one decision.

panel.heading: Keep the numbers trustworthy
items: Daily: record every transaction
Weekly: check cell, Reorder list, unpaid sales
Monthly: count stock, report, back up
Quarterly: review charts, make one decision

say: When you share, choose the lowest access that works. Viewer can only look. Give Editor only to people who really need to type.
Send a lender or partner the report as a PDF, not every customer's name.

panel.heading: Who can see your workbook
items: Give Viewer unless they must type

Protect formula cells

say: If a helper stops working with you, remove their access that same day.

say: To remember. Closing stock is opening plus in minus sold. A reorder level makes your shopping list. VLOOKUP needs FALSE. Net profit is gross profit minus running costs. And keep drawings out of expenses.
